generation.mode: built-in imagegen edit with edit target and canon reference

lighting_isotropy.metric: 36-bin land-luminance-gradient magnitude peak divided by uniform-bin mean on the delivered source; final water-mask pixels excluded and gradients below 12 luminance units excluded
lighting_isotropy.visual_check: No cast-shadow field or time-of-day gradient is visible, but many tussocks and basalt forms retain brighter upper edges or tops and darker lower edges or faces. The numeric aggregate gates pass; the stricter same-value-on-every-side requirement does not.

median_conifer_crown_final_scale.measurement: Manual median full-crown width across 20 representative isolated ordinary conifers, scaled by 2560/1254. A reproducible dark-green component detector found 45 candidates with a 22 source-pixel dark-core median, corroborating that the full crowns are materially underscale.

buildable_vs_steep_fraction.basis: manual estimated fraction of non-water land area
buildable_vs_steep_fraction.method: The broad central clearing and coherent open moor count as buildable; exposed crag and tor faces count as steep; boulder, talus, scrub, gully, and denser conifer ground make up the remainder.

water_mask.encoding: opaque white water pixels on fully transparent non-water pixels; binary alpha
water_mask.derivation: Connected source-raster colour classification over the inspected gully basin, followed by bounded growth through qualifying wet pixels, official blue-fringe admission, morphological closure, component filtering, edge dilation, and enclosed-hole filling. No polyline or hand-drawn shoreline supplied the boundary.

source_scale_gate_proxy.note: The repository blue-leaning classifier was reproduced at source radii that scale to approximately 6 px and 49 px on the 2560 px canvas because node.exe is not exposed in this managed shell.

open_risks: The candidate is not visually compliant with the named rejection defect: repeated bright upper edges and darker lower edges or faces remain on tussocks and basalt despite the aggregate first-moment lighting gate passing.
Median conifer crowns measure about 49.0 px / 2.352 m at final canvas scale, materially below the required 84-147 px / 4-7 m range.
The central dry clearing is broad but does not read as ten correctly scaled 4-7 m conifer crowns wide; the underscale trees make the apparent crown-count misleading.
The main lookout crag and several tors still read as regular upright column bundles with repeated bright tops, contrary to the weathered irregular-basalt rule.
The painting appears to contain more than three pool-like water widenings, including a rock-sheltered side pocket, rather than the requested two or three.
The official Node authoring gates were not run because node.exe is not exposed in the managed shell; the lighting and ring figures are source-scale reproductions using the repository formulas.
Visual seam continuity, exact water-mask judgment, landform naturalism, and terrain quality remain director/owner decisions; mechanical checks do not establish visual acceptance.
